migrationCount124Note: 124 by DBCR-P1-28-001 (20260819090000_rec_damage_map_revision_required.sql), the Owner-QA Backend remediation: rec.guard_damage_map_template_binding() opened with `IF NEW.damage_map_template_version_id IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW`, so every FE-012 rule it states — active slot, live revision, matching document version, matching type and perspective — applied only to a caller that VOLUNTEERED the revision id, and the shipped web client did not. Measured on the running API before the fix: a NEW visit binding a RETIRED template's document pair answered 201 without the field and 422 with it, so the retirement rule was enforced only on a path the product never took. The migration backfills every historical map whose revision is derivable from exactly one (document_id, document_version_id) revision of its tenant — 7 of 7 on the acceptance database, reported by a NOTICE — leaves an ambiguous or underivable row NULL and readable rather than inventing a revision for it, and makes the guard refuse a NULL on INSERT. It is a guard and NOT a NOT NULL column or a NOT VALID CHECK: the invariant is on NEW maps, a column constraint would fail to migrate a database holding an underivable historical row, and a NOT VALID check is still evaluated on UPDATE, which would refuse later maintenance of a legacy NULL row on a table that grants UPDATE to app_runtime.
migrationCount124StructuralNote: structuralTotals and schemaHash are DELIBERATELY unchanged by 124, and that is a measurement rather than an omission. The migration creates no table, no policy and no trigger, and its one CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION replaces an existing function with the same identity — so tables 248, functions 525, policies 649, triggers 551 and security_definer 0 all hold. schemaHash was RE-MEASURED against the database with 124 applied (`npm run validate:schema-inventory -- --hash-only`) and returned 9f536a4641cb97056481f0133d13e42536be0ca1f215717b29842ad04029939a, digit for digit the value already recorded: scripts/db/schema-inventory.mjs hashes function IDENTITY (name and argument types) and not function BODY, so a guard whose rule changed is invisible to it. Stated explicitly because an unchanged hash beside a new migration otherwise reads as a migration that did nothing, and the behaviour change here is proven by tests/db/rec-evidence-contracts.test.ts rather than by a digest.
migrationCountNote: 119 through DBCR-P1-16-001. 120 by DBCR-P1-18-001 (20260731090000_rec_custody_release_visit_marker.sql), which closes P1-27-INT-013 — a Vehicle could be received exactly once, ever, because the terminal status `converted` sat inside the predicate of uq_reception_visits_open_vehicle. 121 by P1-OD-025 (20260815090000_shared_reception_evidence_foundation.sql), the private versioned evidence model. 122 by DBCR-P1-18-002 (20260815093000_rec_receiving_employee_identity.sql), the Owner FE-007 decision: rec.reception_visits.receiving_employee_id carried no foreign key, so any uuid was a legal custodian; it is now a same-tenant reference to iam.user_accounts with an insert-time eligibility guard and an immutable display-name snapshot. 123 by the P1-18 reception evidence contracts (20260815100000_rec_reception_evidence_contracts.sql), the Owner FE-012 / FE-018 / FE-019 decisions: a versioned damage-map template bound to the visit by exact revision, a signature that binds an exact ACCEPTED document version with replacement as new evidence rather than an overwrite, and refusal supporting media optional by default. 121, 122 and 123 were written on THREE separate branches and met in one merge, which is why every figure below is stated as a sum of independently recorded deltas rather than as a single step. 123 REQUIRES 121: it references shared.document_categories.business_link_purpose and the reception_* categories by name and cannot replay without them. 125 by PRE-P1-29-BR-06 (20260826090000_wo_job_work_logs.sql): the progressive work log, which is the FIRST log/note table in the wo/tech/qms/dia schemas — a grep for one across all four returned nothing, so a technician had no way to narrate work beyond a job state and a clock. Typed rather than shared.notes on CONTAINMENT grounds (C-08): shared.notes has NULLABLE company_id/branch_id, so a job note there could carry a NULL branch and containment would move from the row layer into the application. APPEND-ONLY at the GRANT layer — SELECT+INSERT to app_runtime and nothing else, matching dia.diagnostic_evidence and wo.customer_approval_evidence — so an entry cannot be edited or removed, and no UPDATE/DELETE policy exists because adding one for an ungranted verb would suggest the verb does. One composite FK to wo.jobs with its covering index, preserving the measured zero-unindexed-FK property of these four schemas. structuralTotals moves and must be taken from CI. 126 by PRE-P1-29-BR-07 (20260826093000_wo_job_evidence.sql): job-level work evidence, the THIRD instance of a field-identical shape that has already shipped twice (dia.diagnostic_evidence and wo.customer_approval_evidence, correction C-09) — so it is a transcription rather than a design. Parented on wo.jobs and not on the work order (evidence would lose which piece of work it evidences) nor on the assignment (it would vanish when the assignment ended, and work by two successive technicians would split across two parents). APPEND-ONLY at the grant layer, which carries a consequence worth stating: evidence cannot be UNBOUND, so a mis-attached photograph is permanent — the same property both shipped evidence tables have. evidence_type stays FREE TEXT to match its siblings; the vocabulary is an API convention, not a database invariant.
forbiddenMigrationPrefixNote: This reserves a FILENAME series, not an ordinal. It forbids files literally beginning `120` — the `120_`/`120…_` shape a future phase would mint — and it is unrelated to a migration merely being the 120th in the tree. DBCR-P1-18-001 is the 120th migration and is named `20260731090000_…`, so it does not match and this pin stays exactly as it was. Do not 'reconcile' the two numbers: they measure different things, and weakening this to accommodate an ordinal would retire a real guard.

permissionCountNote: 100 through P1-21 and unchanged by P1-22, which declared only codes P1-11 had already seeded. P1-23 raised it to 104 by adding the four READ codes its operations declare: shared.notification.read, shared.notification.delivery.read, shared.document.archive and rpt.report.read. The P1-27 read-surface remediation (executed by P1-18) raised it to 107 with apt.appointment.read, rec.reception.read and rec.reception.close: P1-18 had seeded no read code because it exposed no read operation, and no closure code because closed_without_work/refused were unreachable — both facts that remediation ended (P1-27-INT-010..021, -014, -018, -019). The intake-catalogue MANAGEMENT remediation raises it to 109 with apt.catalogue.manage and rec.catalogue.manage: the seven configuration catalogues ship zero rows by the no-fake-data policy and no operation could add one, so a required appointmentTypeId could never be satisfied — the reads alone did not make the screens usable (P1-27-INT-018). Both are new codes rather than a reuse of apt.appointment.manage / rec.reception.manage, because booking an appointment and defining what the types ARE are different authorities. Added to supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql, which is idempotent and additive — NOT a migration, so migrationCount stays 120 and schemaHash is unchanged. This pin did its job once already: four P1-23 codes were declared by routes and missing from the catalog, and every denial-based authorization test still passed, because a permission that does not exist cannot be held by anybody. P1-OD-025 raises it to 110 with shared.document.read, so reading evidence no longer requires shared.document.manage, the authority that CREATES it. The code is both seeded (04_iam_permission_catalog.sql) and inserted by the migration with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so an environment that migrated without re-seeding still resolves it; both paths are idempotent and the count is one either way. DBCR-P1-18-003 raises it to 112 with rec.reception.evidence.override: waiving a required capture is not the same authority as performing one, so a receptionist who may photograph a vehicle cannot thereby record that no photograph was needed. Seeded and mapped to no role, like every code above it. PRE-P1-29-BR-03 raises it to 113 with tech.technician.manage: the technician roster shipped in P1-19 with reads only, so tech.technician.read was the sole tech.technician code and there was no write authority to gate. Eleven operations now administer profiles, held skills, held certifications and availability windows — the rows GET /technicians/available and assertEligible already consumed and no shipped path could produce — and reading a roster is not administering one, so it is a new code rather than a widening of the read. Added to supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql only: no migration, so migrationCount stays 124 and schemaHash is unchanged. Seeded and mapped to no role, like every code above it. PRE-P1-29-BR-04 raises it to 114 with dia.catalogue.manage: the diagnostics template library had no write path of any kind — dia.inspection_templates, dia.template_versions and dia.template_items all held zero rows and no INSERT existed anywhere in apps/api — so no diagnostic report could be created at all, and closure blocker B4 had an unsatisfiable subject. Authoring what an inspection ASKS is a different authority from recording against one, which is why it is a new high-risk code rather than a widening of dia.diagnostic.record. Seeded and mapped to no role, like every code above it.

structuralTotalsNote: Recorded from the first GitHub-hosted run, using migration-replay-checks.mjs's OWN catalog queries. The earlier note warned that copying earlier phase-gate numbers across would compare two things that were never the same measurement, and run 19 proved that warning exact: `functions` here is 514, while scripts/db/schema-inventory.mjs reported 212 for the same database in the same run.
functionCountDiscrepancyNote: 525 and 223 are both correct; they count different populations, and the difference is entirely in the WHERE clause. migration-replay-checks.mjs counts `pg_proc` filtered only by `n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema')`, so it includes extension and public-namespace functions. schema-inventory.mjs counts `WHERE n.nspname = ANY($1)`, restricted to the 17 RootLco business schemas — and the per-schema breakdown in that same artifact sums to exactly 216 (org, iam, shared, crm, veh, apt, rec, wo, tech, dia, qms, svc, quo, inv, sal, wty, rpt). The 302-function difference is therefore extension-owned code, not RootLco code, and it is constant: the pair moved 514/212 -> 516/214 together when DBCR-P1-18-001 added two rec functions, and 516/214 -> 518/216 when the P1-OD-025 evidence foundation added shared.begin_document_scan and shared.complete_document_scan, then 518/216 -> 519/217 when DBCR-P1-18-002 added rec.stamp_receiving_employee_identity, then 519/217 -> 525/223 when the reception evidence contracts added six rec guards — which is what lets each step be derived rather than guessed. Neither figure was chosen for convenience: 525 belongs HERE because this file is enforced by the script that produces 525, and 223 remains the number to quote for RootLco's own schema and the one comparable with every prior phase gate. Do not 'reconcile' them by editing either.
structuralTotalsCrossChecks: tables 242, triggers 541 and policies 631 are identical under both scripts, and the hosted clean room independently reported 242 live tables, 999 indexes and 537 foreign keys. Only `functions` diverges.
seededStructuralTablesNote: Enumerated from an empty PostgreSQL 17 in run 19 after migrations and seeding, when iam.permissions held 100 rows (104 since P1-23; the row counts below are that run's record, not a pin): iam.permissions (100 rows), inv.units_of_measure (12), sal.payment_methods (3), wo.job_states (6), wo.job_transitions (10), wo.work_order_states (9), wo.work_order_transitions (15). Every one is a structural catalog — permissions, units, payment methods and the work-order state machine — and none is business data, so the no-fake-data policy holds: a freshly provisioned database still starts with no customers, vehicles, orders or invoices. Now that the list is recorded, migration-replay-checks.mjs FAILS on any populated business table outside it, which is the point of recording it. Row counts are deliberately not pinned; the check matches table names only, so seeding one more permission is not a build break.
seededStructuralTablesAsymmetryNote: The check flags UNEXPECTED populated tables, not missing ones. A seed that silently stops running therefore still passes this particular gate — it is caught elsewhere, by the smoke reads and by permissionCount (100 when this note was written, 104 since P1-23 — see permissionCountNote).
securityDefinerPolicyNote: OPEN DECISION, deliberately not resolved on the branch that raised it. scripts/ci/migration-replay-checks.mjs hard-codes security_definer !== 0 as a failure ("the approved count is 0"). That is a rule inside the script, not a value in this file, so it cannot be raised by editing the baseline. Migration 20260815090000 adds TWO: shared.begin_document_scan and shared.complete_document_scan. Both pin an empty search_path, both are REVOKEd from PUBLIC and GRANTed only to app_runtime, and both re-check tenant, actor, permission and source state on every call. They exist because the alternative is worse: granting app_runtime INSERT on shared.file_scan_results would let request code write its own clean verdict, which is exactly the withholding that keeps accepted out of reach of request code and which three existing suites assert. Somebody must choose between raising the approved count to 2 with this justification recorded, moving the scan to the app_worker role, or accepting the weaker grant. Nothing was weakened unilaterally.
structuralTotalsDeltaNote3: DBCR-P1-18-003 (the reception evidence contracts) raises `tables` 242 -> 248, `functions` 519 -> 525, `policies` 633 -> 649 and `triggers` 544 -> 551. The deltas are read off the migration and CONFIRMED against the rebuilt catalogue, which is the only reason they can be stated rather than guessed: six CREATE TABLE, six CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, seven CREATE TRIGGER and sixteen CREATE POLICY, and `tests/db/foundation.test.ts` independently reported exactly those six routines, seven triggers and sixteen policies as absent from its declared inventories before they were added. `security_definer` stays 0: every one of the six guards is SECURITY INVOKER with an empty search_path, which the same suite asserts. These four totals still cannot be reproduced on a developer stack — it carries auth/storage/realtime objects the CI plain-postgres container does not — so CI settles them; the schemaHash beside them IS locally reproducible and was re-measured against a database carrying all 123 migrations.
